questions.question: After a release, LCP regressed on mobile. How do you investigate end-to-end?
questions.title: LCP Regression After Deploy — Investigation Playbook
questions.direct_answer:
After a release, LCP regressed on mobile. How do you investigate end-to-end?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** RUM vs lab, LCP element attribution, INP interaction, regressions tied to deploy diff (bundle size, third parties).

**Classic weak answer:** Optimizing CLS or FID when the metric that moved is LCP — chasing the wrong Core Web Vital.

**Senior finish:** Mention **fetchpriority=high**, **preload** for critical LCP image, **HTTP cache/CDN** for HTML, and **feature flag rollback** while you bisect.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **LCP Regression After Deploy — Investigation Playbook** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** After a release, LCP regressed on mobile. How do you investigate end-to-end?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **RUM vs lab, LCP element attribution, INP interaction, regressions tied to deploy diff (bundle size, third parties)**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Optimizing CLS or FID when the metric that moved is LCP — chasing the wrong Core Web Vital**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention **fetchpriority=high**, **preload** for critical LCP image, **HTTP cache/CDN** for HTML, and **feature flag rollback** while you bisect**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** RUM vs lab, LCP element attribution, INP interaction, regressions tied to deploy diff (bundle size, third parties)
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **optimizing CLS or FID when the metric that moved is LCP — chasing the wrong Core Web Vital** and what you do instead.

- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **RUM vs lab, LCP element attribution, INP interaction, regressions tied to deploy diff (bundle size, third parties)** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Optimizing CLS or FID when the metric that moved is LCP — chasing the wrong Core Web Vital** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention **fetchpriority=high**, **preload** for critical LCP image, **HTTP cache/CDN** for HTML, and **feature flag rollback** while you bisect**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: We ship a large SPA. How do you balance SEO and client-side performance?
questions.title: SEO + SPA — Prerender, SSR, and Crawl Budget
questions.direct_answer:
We ship a large SPA. How do you balance SEO and client-side performance?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** When CSR is acceptable, hybrid models (SSG islands + SPA shell), canonical/hreflang, structured data delivery.

**Classic weak answer:** Duplicating thin pages for every query string without canonicals — SEO noise and crawl waste.

**Senior finish:** Reference **meta rendering in RSC/App Router**, **edge SSR**, and **partial prerendering** as modern hybrids.
